text:
Alex: Heads-up: customer on Android hit auth failures when following redirects. We saw 302 from /login -> auth.example.com and the subsequent request lost Authorization header, causing 401s. Repro in our sample-app using Retrofit+OkHttp.
Priya: OkHttp intentionally strips Authorization on cross-host redirects for safety. Are the redirect and final host different?
Alex: Yes. Flow: app calls API -> receives 302 to auth.example.com with a token-in-query (legacy) -> client follows redirect automatically. The redirected request to auth.example.com should be unauthenticated, but our SDK was expecting to attach cookie/session header and it wasn't there. Some requests ended up 401 because server expected the Authorization header on the follow-up.
Sam: Two issues: (1) automatic redirect semantics differ across platforms and OkHttp purposely drops sensitive headers when hostname changes, (2) Retrofit callers sometimes assume followRedirects will keep headers.
Oleg: For SDK guidance: don't rely on default followRedirects for auth flows. Either handle redirects manually at app layer or use a custom interceptor to reapply or transform headers when redirecting. Example interceptor to reattach safe headers on same-origin or to handle auth-redirects explicitly:
```kotlin
.addInterceptor { chain ->
  val req = chain.request()
  val resp = chain.proceed(req)
  if ((resp.code == 302 || resp.code == 301) && shouldRewriteRedirect(req, resp)) {
    val location = resp.header("Location") ?: return@addInterceptor resp
    val newReq = req.newBuilder()
      .url(location)
      // reattach any app-specific header we consider safe for that target
      .header("X-Client-Session", sessionStore.current())
      .build()
    resp.close()
    return@addInterceptor chain.proceed(newReq)
  }
  resp
}
```
Katy: Also note TLS/host change rules: OkHttp will remove Authorization when host changes to avoid leaking credentials. If your backend expects auth across a redirect, the correct fix is to have the server issue a 307 (preserve method and headers semantics) or use a cookie-based single-sign-on flow.
Priya: For the SDK sample-apps we should add a test that verifies redirect behavior across origins and document the recommended fix: manual redirect handling or server-side 307/308 for auth flows.
Sam: Add a short dev note in mobile onboarding: "Don't assume headers survive cross-host redirects" and show the interceptor snippet + server alternatives.
Alex: Filed internal issue and pushed a failing repro test to sample-apps. For now we added a quick fix in the app using the interceptor above and updated docs. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
